title: Lost and Found
tagline: A 100% AI-generated short film — and a proof of concept for AI-native brand storytelling.

body: AI video carries a stigma: people assume it can't look good, and that it's limited to slow zooms and sci-fi landscapes. For brands, that perception is the real barrier — nobody wants their story to look like a tech demo. I set out to break it with camera work that felt natural and cinematic, in service of a story that felt grounded and real.

Most AI content online is a string of short clips with no depth or meaning. I wanted to show what happens when you bring a creative director's discipline to the tools: a real story, a fully realized world and characters an audience could care about, built with nothing but text-to-video prompting.

feature.caption: Lost and Found — AI short film.

body: I gave myself six days to make a 100% AI-generated short film — to learn the tools firsthand, find their limits, and work out a repeatable process I could bring to brand and marketing work.

I wrote and storyboarded a post-apocalyptic thriller following a dog, a robot and a little girl on a haunting journey. Using a range of tools — primarily Google's Veo 2 — I generated every clip, spending much of the process on prompt-engineering R&D to keep characters and environments consistent from shot to shot, the same way a brand world has to hold together across a campaign.
led: Wrote, storyboarded and directed the film
Built a prompt-engineering process for character and world consistency

impact.note: Posted on LinkedIn, the film passed a million impressions and 100+ shares and reposts within the week, and brought several new job opportunities. The process now shapes how I approach AI-native storytelling for brands.
